Chapter One: Ordinary Beginnings and Unseen Shadows.
Sometimes, the most unsettling truths are right there in plain sight—woven into the fabric of our daily lives, so familiar we hardly notice.
Picture this: it's the early 1970s in Seattle. A woman is working late nights at a crisis hotline center, answering call after call from people standing on the edge. The work is tough. You need a steady hand, a calm voice, and a heart that doesn’t break easily.
But she wasn’t alone. Sitting beside her, night after night, was a young man who just seemed to glow with warmth and intelligence. He was the kind of person you'd want nearby—attentive, quick to help, always ready with a reassuring word for someone in trouble. If you’d watched them together, you might've thought, “Now, that’s someone I’d trust. That’s someone I’d want as a friend.” He seemed reliable, charming, deeply empathetic.
This was life before the headlines. Before any horror stories. Just two colleagues sharing stories, laughter, and those late-night moments that only happen when you’re facing tough situations together. The young man, with his easy smile and gentle manner, looked like everything good about humanity. He talked about his dreams, his studies in psychology, and how he wanted to make a difference. Nothing about him felt off. Not even a little.
But then, over time, something changed. A string of disturbing events started to ripple through the city. Young women began disappearing. First one, then another—gone, with no clues left behind. Seattle grew anxious; parents worried every time their daughters left home. Rumors spread like wildfire. And yet, for those who knew the man at the hotline, the thought that he could be involved? It just didn’t make sense. He was just like everyone else—maybe even better.
We like to think evil announces itself, right? That it shows up with a scowl or an obvious warning sign. But most of us don’t notice the subtle hints—the little inconsistencies that whisper something’s not quite right. In the comfortable routine of everyday life, it’s easy to trust those who seem familiar, to brush off the odd moments that don’t fit the pattern. The woman at the hotline found herself stuck in that in-between space—torn between what she saw and what she felt, unable to match her friend’s kindness with the growing sense of unease that crept in with every new disappearance.
As the investigation heated up, the city’s sense of safety started to slip away. Police were searching for answers, but it was slow going—no digital databases, no DNA analysis, just old-fashioned police work and a lot of intuition. The community watched in horror as the list of missing women grew longer, and each case became more puzzling. The fear was real. But so was the disbelief. How could something so violent be hiding right alongside the ordinary rhythm of daily life?
Through it all, the woman at the hotline hung on to her belief: her friend couldn’t possibly be involved. She remembered his kindness, his gentle patience with callers in crisis, the way he always seemed to know just what to say. But here’s something to pay attention to—sometimes, trust can cut both ways. The very qualities that made him seem so trustworthy? They were the same ones that let him move through the world unnoticed, hiding his true self behind a careful mask.
So, what do we learn from those first years? That evil doesn’t always come with a warning. Sometimes, it’s sitting right beside us, blending in so perfectly we never think to look twice. The lesson, learned the hard way by so many, is that staying watchful and a little skeptical isn’t cynical—it’s the wisdom that comes from experience.
